changes: Costs the Octatrack nothing while nothing in the project uses FM Synth: it rests until a track does.
An FM track in any Part, a legacy FMSYNTH sample in any slot or GLIDE turned on keeps it awake. Picking FM SYNTH wakes it at once.
Known issue: an FM track that has played notes keeps costing CPU while silent or stopped. A fix will follow.
Its CPU price is now 4 % of a frame a track (was 6), so the CPU budget no longer refuses an FM Synth track on its own. A busy unit can still refuse one.
Sound and controls are unchanged.
FM Synth now tells the Octatrack what one track of it costs: 6 % of a frame.
A Part now takes FM Synth on up to seven tracks; before, the fourth was refused with CPU FULL. A unit that is already busy can still refuse one sooner.
Sound and controls are unchanged.
The limit applies on Modwerk base 0.7 and later.
FM Synth takes far less of the unit's CPU while it is installed and on no track. Its sound and controls are unchanged.
On an MKII with four sample tracks playing it took about 3 points of the frame interrupt on no track, down from 19.
Fixes track 1's LFO 3, which did nothing while FM Synth was installed.
Checked on an MKII by recording one FM Synth track against 0.1.2. Known issue: chords, glide and MIDI are not yet checked on hardware.
Fixes the instrument stopping responding after changing the MIDI trig mode (#264).
Adds headroom so FM Synth no longer clips inside the machine (#273). It is about 18 dB quieter at the same mixer settings; effects and the mix can still clip.
Installs over USB beside every other module on the Modwerk beta base. Removing it after playing no longer crashes the unit.
Media and documentation only: adds a melodic audio preview, and notes that ATK 0 with a short HOLD or REL can click (#557) and that LFO1/LFO2 show FLEX's destination names (#589).
Known issue: this version has not been tested on hardware.
First Modwerk release of FM Synth, an SRC track machine that needs no sample.
Supports one to four voices, chords, glide and parameter locks.
Known issue: not yet tested on hardware.
